Read both changed files in the workspace and the reference. Here is my plan.

## Which files differ

Two files differ between the current version the user has and the target version:

- `src/packaging/metadata.py` — the part that checks the content type of a package's description.
- `tests/test_metadata.py` — the examples that say which description content types are accepted and which are rejected.

## What is wrong or missing in the current version

In `src/packaging/metadata.py` (workspace, around the description content type check), the code reads the charset from the description content type and compares it to the exact spelling `UTF-8`. If the spelling is anything else, the library reports the value as not allowed. So `utf-8` (small letters) and `Utf-8` (mixed) are treated as wrong, even though they name the same thing as `UTF-8`.

In `tests/test_metadata.py` (workspace), the list of values that are expected to be rejected includes `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, and the list of values that are expected to work only has `text/plain; charset=UTF-8`.

In the reference, the comparison ignores letter case (`.lower()` is used, comparing to `utf-8`), the lowercase spelling is moved to the accepted examples, `Utf-8` is added as accepted, and a new example that reads package details from text with the lowercase spelling is added.

## Files in the WORKSPACE that are about the problem (for Hints)

- `src/packaging/metadata.py`
- `tests/test_metadata.py`

## Ticket section outline (plain words, no code)

Title: Description content type with lowercase charset spelling is rejected.

- What happens now: When a package description says its content type uses the charset spelled `utf-8` in small letters, the library treats that as an error and says the value is not allowed. Only the exact spelling `UTF-8` is accepted.
- What should happen: The spelling of the charset should not matter. `utf-8`, `Utf-8`, and `UTF-8` should all be treated the same way and accepted.
- About this project: This project is a set of tools for reading and checking Python package information, including the details that describe a package such as its name, version, and description content type. It gives clear results and clear errors when package details are read.
- Problem this solves: Many real packages write the charset in small letters. Today the tool refuses those packages even though they are fine, so the user is blocked from reading perfectly good package details.
- What changed: The new version accepts any letter casing of the charset spelling for the description content type, and the examples show the small-letter and mixed-letter spellings as accepted.
- Impact: Correctness and usability. Fewer valid packages are turned away, and error messages stop appearing for values that are actually fine.
- User experience: Today, reading a package whose description content type says `text/plain; charset=utf-8` gives an error. In the new version, the same package reads without error and the description content type is kept as written.
- Hints: `src/packaging/metadata.py`, `tests/test_metadata.py`

{"file_path": "/megabit/ticket.md", "content": "# Packages that spell the letter set for their description as small letters are turned away

## What happens now

When I read the details of a package and its description says the letter set is written as "utf-8" in small letters, the tool refuses it and reports an error saying that only UTF-8 is allowed. Only the exact spelling "UTF-8" in capital letters is let through, even though "utf-8" and "Utf-8" mean the very same thing.

## What should happen

The way the letters are capitalized should not matter. I should be able to read package details no matter whether the letter set is written as "utf-8", "Utf-8", or "UTF-8", and the value should be kept as the package wrote it.

## About this project

This project gives people a set of tools for reading and checking the information that describes a Python package, such as its name, version, and the text that explains it. It reads those details and either hands them back clearly or explains what is not allowed. People use it to look at packages before trusting or shipping them.

## Problem this solves

Many real packages write the letter set in small letters, and they are perfectly fine packages. Today the tool turns those packages away and shows an error, which blocks me from reading and using details that are actually valid.

## What changed

Now the spelling of the letter set no longer matters: small letters, mixed letters, and capital letters are all treated the same way and accepted. The old behavior of only accepting the capital-letter spelling is gone. The examples that come with the project now show "utf-8" and "Utf-8" as accepted and no longer list "utf-8" as an error.

## Impact

Correctness and ease of use.

## User experience

Before: I read a package whose description says "text/plain; charset=utf-8", and I get an error telling me that value is not allowed. After: I read the very same package and it works, with the description kept just as the package wrote it.

## Hints

- /workspace/src/packaging/metadata.py
- /workspace/tests/test_metadata.py"}
